reviewer: Codex parent session; independent of the fixture-generation invocation

findings.bullet: - app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — The diff deletes `app/defaults.json`, but `app/startup.py:6` still resolves it via `Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text()`, and nothing in the diff repoints that loader at the new `load_config`; grep shows `defaults.json` has no other provider. — Any call to `load_defaults()` now raises `FileNotFoundError`, so application startup fails outright.
findings.reason: Names the deleted defaults file, its unchanged load_defaults consumer, and FileNotFoundError on invocation; the base-side citation matches the deletion.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port` returns `0 < p < 65535`, which yields `False` for `p = 65535`, the highest legal TCP port, while the docstring on line 21 states the usable range is "(1-65535)"; the upper comparison needs `<=`. — Callers using this helper reject a valid port (e.g. a service bound to 65535) as invalid.
findings.reason: Identifies input 65535 and the exclusive upper bound, explaining rejection of a valid TCP port.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `load_config` wraps the open-and-parse in `except Exception: return {}` with no logging, no caller signal, and no comment or docstring noting the fallback, so a missing file, a permissions error, and malformed JSON (e.g. a config with a trailing comma) are indistinguishable from an intentionally empty config. — An operator who typos the config path or corrupts the JSON gets a silently empty configuration and no message explaining why their settings were ignored.
findings.reason: Names realistic file/JSON errors that become an indistinguishable empty configuration, with no caller diagnostic.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring says `normalize_host` "returns None when h is empty", but the code at lines 36-37 returns `""` for that input: `if h == "": return ""`. — A caller following the documented contract and testing `if normalize_host(h) is None` never detects the empty-host case and proceeds with `""` as a real hostname.
findings.reason: Contrasts the promised None with the actual empty-string result and explains how callers checking for None are misled.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:38 — tests — The added `test_normalize_host_lowercases` passes `"Example.COM"`, for which `h.endswith(".")` is `False`, so the trailing-dot stripping branch (`h = h[:-1]`) has no test; a fully-qualified input like `"Example.COM."` exercises it and is asserted nowhere. — The documented dot-stripping behavior could break or be inverted without any test failing.
findings.reason: Identifies the untested trailing-dot branch and a concrete stripping regression that the existing lowercase-only test misses; credit is for that distinct branch.

findings.bullet: - app/parse.py:29 — tests — `load_config`'s success path (`_fastjson.loads(f.read())` returning a parsed dict for a valid file) has no test in `tests/test_parse.py`, which imports only `parse_timeout` and `normalize_host`. — A regression in the config read, including one specific to the `ujson`/`json` accelerator swap, would ship undetected.
findings.reason: The valid-JSON success path also has no test; this is a separate regression risk from the swallowed-error defect and does not increase planted-defect recall.
